tier_rule: the highest tier whose threshold the score meets or exceeds
evidence_rule: every yes or partial needs an evidence_quote that appears verbatim in the redacted CV; otherwise the level is no
excluded_from_scoring: employer vs personal project (judge the depth of the work, not where it was done)

requirements.text: Python for applications or data pipelines, with engineering practice
requirements.yes: Python used in applications or pipelines with evidence of engineering practice: tests, packaging, CI or production use
requirements.partial: Python scripting, basic use or coursework only

requirements.text: Built an application on an LLM API, beyond basic prompting
requirements.yes: An application calling an LLM API with depth: structured outputs or schema validation, an evaluation, or real users
requirements.partial: A basic LLM application (prompting only, such as a simple chatbot or summariser). Using a chat UI such as ChatGPT is 'no'

requirements.yes: Built retrieval over documents (embeddings + vector store feeding an LLM) with depth: retrieval evaluation, tuning such as chunking, or real users
requirements.partial: A basic embeddings/RAG project without evaluation or tuning, or coursework on the topic

requirements.yes: Designed a test set or evaluation: held-out data, metrics and error analysis
requirements.partial: Reported a metric without describing how the evaluation was designed

requirements.yes: Built and exposed REST endpoints with a web framework (FastAPI, Flask, Spring Boot, Express or similar)
requirements.partial: A single basic or personal endpoint

requirements.yes: Uses Git or a Git-based CI (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI)
Built an agent or a tool-calling workflow
requirements.partial: Used LLM frameworks such as LangChain without tools or agents

requirements.yes: Deployed or ran a service on a cloud platform

partial_null_means: this requirement has no partial level: yes or no only
